Hi Ben,

What we need to balance: predictable monthly spend for finance, a short-term uplift for the launch window (72 hours), and a reasonable true-up that doesn't blow our cash flow. I attached a short forecast and the usage snapshot from 11/16.

Thanks for the context and the files, Alicia — quick read looks straightforward. A couple quick proposals to consider (short list so it’s easy to decide):

1) Short-window prepaid cushion: BrightFence prepays a one-time cushion equal to 30% of committed monthly throughput (applied for 14 days post-launch). Any unused portion converts to invoice credit applied over next two billing cycles. No change to base commit price; cushion is a consumption credit.

2) Temporary rate-limit upgrade + prorated true-up: Provide a 2x rate-limit uplift for a 72-hour window (managed via our routing policy) — usage during uplift billed at current overrun rate but we cap net uplift cost with a 25% cap rebate on overrun tokens if you accept a 3-month runway commit.

3) Staged true-up with discount: For the overage in question, convert 50% to an amortized true-up spread over 3 invoices, and offer a one-time 7% credit on that amortized portion if you commit to a 2-month minimum increase after the launch.

I’m copying Karthik and Jordan to confirm feasibility and to get a quick sense of pricing math and legal redline risk. If any of those look promising I’ll draft a short addendum we can sign (DocuSign).

—Ben

Subject: Re: Unexpected overage last month — options to smooth? — pricing sketch

Ben — thanks for laying out options. Quick feasibility/pricing sketch from infra and pricing POV:

- Option 1 (Prepaid cushion): technically simple, low legal friction. Recommend: cushion = 25% of typical month (they currently commit ~1.2B tokens/mo) => ~300M-token cushion, valid for 14 days. We suggest a 60% refund conversion for unused cushion to discourage gaming (i.e., 40% forfeited if unused).

- Option 2 (Rate-limit upgrade + cap rebate): we can expose a temporary policy to allow 2x QPS for 72 hrs. For economics, propose rebate structure: if BrightFence signs a 3-month 10% commit uplift, rebate 25% on overrun billing for the uplift window (cap $12k). Without commit uplift, overrun billed standard. This protects Redwood exposure.

- Option 3 (Staged true-up + discount): operationally easiest for finance; propose amortize over 3 invoices, offer 8% credit on amortized portion in exchange for a 2-month commit increase.

My recommendation: start with Option 1 + Option 2 combo: cushion to smooth finance in the short-window + temporary QPS uplift for launch. If they want to avoid a one-time cushion payment, we can offer the amortized true-up (Option 3) instead with the 8% credit.

If we go forward, Jordan can route to legal for a lightweight addendum we use for pilot launches. Jordan — can you confirm legal okay with the 60%/40% refund language and cap language for the rebate?

—Karthik

- Cushion: we prefer a refundable cushion with 80% return of unused funds (not 60%). We’re happy to prepay for the cushion if the refund rate is higher.
- Rate-limit upgrade: we need 2x QPS for a 72-hour window around launch (agree with policy control). We also need the ability to pause the upgrade if errors spike — is that acceptable?
- Discount/commit trade: BrightFence will sign a 3-month 10% increase in commit (for launch and stabilization) in exchange for 20% rebate on overrun billing incurred during the 72-hour uplift window (cap $10k).

Attached: revised forecast and a short note from finance re: how they prefer amortization. If you can send a one-page addendum (we prefer DocuSign), we’ll get legal to review quickly.
